title: After an admission timeout, a Work turn stays queued in an empty queue
description:
A supervising agent cannot tell whether to wait or retry. We observed this on 2026-11-24 UTC after a GEDS backend run processed 189,994 CSV rows and passed 18 focused tests. We could verify the import in tool output, but could not hand off a commit.

Observed
1. The original turn reported running while the conversation was idle and steer returned 409 no_active_turn. Recovery reported a time limit. A recovery retry briefly restored execution. At 02:13 UTC the turn settled as failed. Its retained reply contained only the opening progress message.
2. At 02:14 UTC a follow-up to preserve the changes was accepted at queue position 1. After an admission timeout, turns still showed it as queued, with queuePosition null, queueDepth 0, activeTurnID null and phase idle. Recovery offered no actions. The follow-up had no retained reply. Repeating the submission with the same idempotency key returned HTTP 503.

Expected
An accepted turn should remain in the queue, start running, or reach an explicit terminal state with the cause and a safe next action. The CLI should surface pending permissions and settlement blockers while waiting. A retry using the same key should identify the original turn and its disposition, so the operator can avoid duplicate work.

Suggested regression test
Use a disposable workspace. Queue a follow-up while its predecessor settles, then simulate a timeout during admission. Check turns, status, wait, recovery and replay with the same key. Assert the follow-up is either runnable or terminal and that it can execute at most once.
